notable_findings: AccessGUDID and openFDA /device/udi.json publish the SAME GUDID record: the same DI (00643169718425) returns the same publicDeviceRecordKey on both interfaces, so they are one evidence item and must be de-duplicated, never counted as two sources.

US device identity and US clearance identity are officially joinable - from the UDI side only: GUDID premarket_submissions names the K/PMA number (verified DI 00643169718425 -> K973011), while a 510(k)/PMA record carries no DI, model or labeler id at all.

Health Canada MDALL is the only non-US source found that exposes an official UDI-DI endpoint (/deviceidentifier/?device_identifier=), but it returned 0 rows for a US-only Medtronic DI - the bridge exists and is sparse, not universal.

MDALL exposes exactly three dates per licence (first_licence_status_dt, last_refresh_dt, end_date); the refresh stamp and the cancellation date are precisely the two the protocol forbids as first-publication dates, so MDALL source_public_at can only ever be a derived proxy.

GUDID daily release files are self-describing in a way no live API is: header creationDate + period start/end + numberRecordXML (5,548, matching the 5,548 records actually parsed), which is what makes point-in-time reconstruction possible.

openFDA applicant search resolves all five target firms by exact_alias: 510(k) totals Medtronic 1,588 / Philips 994 / GE HealthCare 266 / Mindray 180 / Drager 152; PMA totals Medtronic 12,900 / Philips 169 / GE HealthCare 55, and PMA returns 404 (zero rows) for Drager and Mindray - they hold no PMA approvals at all.

The openFDA bulk manifest carries a real per-endpoint export_date (2026-11-02..06) and is the only way to pin a defensible vintage; the API's meta.last_updated is an endpoint refresh stamp that would silently re-date every record.

A classification record has no date of any kind - FDA publishes the current value of a product code with no effective date, so its clocks must stay empty or every historical clearance inherits today's risk class.

MDALL company counts are %LIKE% matches, so they include unrelated subsidiaries - company linkage goes through CompanyIndex, not the substring hit.

open_questions: EUDAMED: worth registering for the DG SANTE EU Health Data Lake Data API (api=94b9e658-d721-4b58-8d96-022c490f7a17)? Without it the EU has no device data and the EU-vs-US registration-timing comparison cannot be built.
TGA: whether the timeouts are this host's egress or a TGA-side block. Re-probing from another network would settle it; if the Akamai probe is served again, the source stays blocked by policy.

PMA supplements: the connector deliberately uses a pma_supplement identifier so canonical_key does not collapse every supplement of an approval into one key. Lead should confirm that dedupe convention before downstream aggregation across sources.

GUDID: does devicePublishDate ever change for an existing record? Only a multi-day delta study can answer that, and it decides whether devicePublishDate is a stable publication clock or a first-seen stamp.
Cross-country DI matching currently works for exactly one non-US market (Canada). EUDAMED and NMPA would be the second and third, and both are blocked for different reasons.
